newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST - DEBT CUTS, FOOD TO BOOST PREMIER.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - DEBT CUTS, FOOD TO BOOST PREMIER.

text.p: A major debt reduction and a revamp of its food operations will be the main drivers behind an expected 30 percent leap in year earnings at South African food to pharmaceuticals firm Premier Group Ltd, analysts said on Friday.

Analysts said that subsidiary Metro Cash & Carry Ltd (Metcash) will make a sturdy contribution to group earnings, but that this will be offset by poor showings at other units, Bonnita Holdings Ltd and CNA Gallo Ltd .
Premier is due to report results for the 12 months to April 30 next Wednesday.

The beginnings of a turnaround seen at the 1996 financial year end at Premier Foods, which houses interests ranging from milling and baking to fishing and oils, will gather steam after its dismal performance in previous years, analysts said.
"The foods business has been better positioned and the restructure has improved efficiencies," said Carolyn Windsor, an analyst at Investec Securities.
Premier Foods, which was seen posting profits of around 115 million rand from 95.6 million rand in 1996, would benefit from a big cut in group debt after last year's 456 million rights issue.

Other corrective measures taken at the foods unit, which in 1995 posted a loss of 63.1 million rand, include the sale of a stake in retailer Clicks Ltd, the appointment of a new chief executive and the sale of other non-core and property assets.
But other analysts said Premier Foods still had a long way to go before it could diagnosed as healthy.

"It is still under some pressure from relatively high levels of debt, high interest rates and the restructuring which has dampened the morale of some employees," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.

Analysts polled by Reuters forecast group headline earnings for the year to end April rising to between 38.5 cents and 40 cents a share with consensus at 39.4 -- a surge of 31.3 percent above the 30.0 cents reported a year ago.
They expected the dividend to come in a range of 14.2 to 17.0 cents with consensus at 15.4. The 1996 year dividend was 12.5 cents.

Premier overall will be puffed up by a 25 percent jump in Metcash's year earnings and an expected 20 percent rise in earnings for the year to end-September at pharmaceutical group Adcock Ingram Ltd , which last year merged with Premier Pharmaceuticals.

But other listed units retailer CNA and dairy firm Bonnita will weigh after both reported lower earnings, the former hard hit by the tight interest rate enviroment and the latter by a shortage of milk.
Unlisted pharmaceutical unit United Pharmaceutical Holdings is expected to show modest earnings growth of some 18 percent.
